hardware_summary: 18 MW gas-turbine-based captive power plant (CPP) -- the terminal's primary power source, with Gujarat State grid (66 kV, from a substation ~10 km away) as standby, and an emergency diesel generator as a further backup for CPP-and-grid failure.
fuel_basis: Regasified/send-out natural gas fires the Gas Turbine Generator (GTG); per the project's Risk Assessment/EIA report, three power-source configurations were evaluated (grid+gas-engine backup, gas-engine+grid backup, gas-turbine+grid backup) and gas-turbine-based generation of 18 MW was the selected configuration.
captive_summary: Chhara LNG Terminal's Risk Assessment / EIA report (filed by HPCL/HPLNG with India's environmental clearance authority) states the terminal's power will be supplied from an 18 MW captive power plant (CPP) using a Gas Turbine Generator, with the Gujarat State 66 kV grid as standby supply and an emergency diesel generator for CPP+grid failure. Heat recovered from the GTG exhaust also feeds an LNG vaporizer (STV) heat-recovery loop.
confirmed_how: The project's Risk Assessment report (filed on India's environmentclearance.nic.in portal for the HPCL/HPLNG Chhara LNG terminal, Gir Somnath, Gujarat) states: 'CPP configuration with Gas Turbine based Power Generation of 18 MW capacity is selected'; and 'Power will be supplied from 18 MW captive power plant with a provision of standby supply from nearest Gujarat State electric grid power supply of 66 KV available from Substation at Sarkhadi village, approx. 10 km from Project site. In case of failure of CPP and Grid supply, Emergency Diesel Generator will be used.' This is a primary regulatory filing, sufficient alone for a green verdict.
